intro: The Colts started their teardown by sending Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. Sunday brings Lamar Jackson back against Buffalo and the league's lone unbeaten, Minnesota, into Detroit. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Colts trade Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to San Francisco
top.dek: Indianapolis moved both veterans days after it fired GM Chris Ballard. Seattle sent a 2027 third and a 2028 fifth for Nelson, and San Francisco sent a 2027 fourth for Buckner. Both players were in the final year of their deals.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Lamar Jackson set to return from high ankle sprain against Buffalo
top.dek: Jackson took full reps Wednesday and Thursday and practiced again Friday after missing three games. Coach Jesse Minter said the team expects to have him. Guard Olaivavega Ioane and safety Jaylinn Hawkins are out.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Matthew Stafford passes Roman Gabriel for the Rams touchdown record
top.dek: Stafford threw three touchdown passes in a 35-21 win at Las Vegas. That gave him 155 as a Ram, one more than Gabriel's 154. Davis Allen caught two of them, a career high.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 154.3: Bears rushing yards per game, tops in the NFL
top.dek: No team runs for more yards per game than Chicago. The defense also holds opponents to a 26 percent third-down conversion rate. Both units face Seattle on Monday night.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Unbeaten Vikings visit the Lions Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
top.dek: Minnesota is 6-0 with the league's top defense by EPA and an offense ranked 31st. Detroit has the second-ranked offense but plays without Kerby Joseph. Watch Aidan Hutchinson against the Vikings' protection.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills return from bye to face Lamar and Ravens

stories.text: Bills come off the bye to host a Ravens team getting Lamar Jackson back
stories.summary: Buffalo sits at 5-1 and plays its first game after a week off under coach Joe Brady. Baltimore's Lamar Jackson practiced in full this week after an ankle injury and looks set to play. Damar Hamlin should start at safety because CJ Gardner-Johnson serves a one-game suspension.

stories.text: Six Bills carry questionable tags, led by DJ Moore
stories.summary: Receiver DJ Moore (shoulder), tight end Dalton Kincaid (chest), cornerback Dee Alford (ankle), lineman Greg Gaines (back), tackle Spencer Brown (back) and linebacker TJ Parker (knee) are all questionable for Sunday. Lineman Ed Oliver has no designation and should play for the first time since Week 4. Receiver Tyrell Shavers (knee) stays on injured reserve this week.

stories.text: James Cook sits third in the NFL in rushing
stories.summary: Cook enters Week 8 with 627 rushing yards, third most in the league. He anchors the ground game for a 5-1 Buffalo team coming off the bye.

stories.text: 11: Derrick Henry touchdowns in seven career games against Buffalo
stories.summary: Henry has scored 11 times in seven games against the Bills. Since he joined Baltimore, he has four touchdowns and 368 rushing yards in two meetings with Buffalo. Stopping him is the first job for the Bills defense.

stories.text: Ravens at Highmark Stadium, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo (5-1) hosts Baltimore (4-3) on Sunday, Nov. 1. The teams met in Week 1 of 2025, a 41-40 Bills win. Watch whether Moore and Kincaid suit up and how Buffalo handles Henry.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins beat Jets for first win, host Patriots

stories.text: Dolphins edge Jets 28-25 for their lone win of the season
stories.summary: Miami won on the road at MetLife Stadium on Oct. 25 and sits at 1-5. The offense ran for a score and passed for two more, while safety Michael Taaffe intercepted Geno Smith. The team then claimed guard Christian Haynes off waivers from Seattle.

stories.text: Kadyn Proctor out with a concussion, two corners questionable
stories.summary: Guard and tackle Kadyn Proctor will miss Sunday's game. Cornerbacks JuJu Brents (neck, concussion) and Reese Taylor (quad) are questionable, though both practiced fully on Friday. Quarterback Malik Willis (groin) and running back Jaylen Wright (foot, quad) also practiced fully.

stories.text: Malik Willis accounts for three scores in the win over the Jets
stories.summary: Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns, then added 37 yards and a touchdown on eight carries. He is also dealing with a groin injury but practiced fully on Friday.

stories.text: 6: sacks by the Dolphins, last in the NFL
stories.summary: Miami also ranks last in EPA per pass allowed at 0.28. The pass rush gets a test against a Patriots offense led by Drake Maye, who ranks first in EPA per play over the last four weeks.

stories.text: Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami hosts New England on Nov. 1. The Patriots have lost seven of their last nine games in Miami, and their defense has allowed the league's worst quarterback rating in zone coverage. Watch whether Miami's run game keeps working.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots monitor A.J. Brown before Miami trip

stories.text: Patriots head to Miami with A.J. Brown questionable
stories.summary: Brown is listed with an ankle and knee injury after playing 101 combined snaps against the Jets and Bears in five days. New England sits at 4-3 and is trying to win in Miami, where it has lost seven of its last nine games.

stories.text: Brown and Henderson did not practice Friday
stories.summary: Receiver A.J. Brown (ankle, knee) and running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice and are questionable. Cornerback Carlton Davis III (neck) and linebacker Christian Elliss (chest) are also questionable but practiced fully. Quarterback Drake Maye (right shoulder) was a full participant.

stories.text: Hunter Henry piles up catches over the last four weeks
stories.summary: The tight end has 19 receptions for 225 yards and two touchdowns across the last four games. Drake Maye leads the league in EPA per play over the same stretch, and Henry is one of his main targets.

stories.text: 25: missed tackles by the Patriots over Weeks 6 and 7
stories.summary: New England missed 25 tackles across its last two games. The defense also grades poorly in zone coverage, with the league's worst quarterback rating allowed in that look.

stories.text: Patriots at Dolphins, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: New England (4-3) visits Miami (1-5) at Hard Rock Stadium on Nov. 1. Watch Brown's status and whether the defense cleans up its tackling.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets drop to 2-5 and host Raiders

stories.text: Jets fall 28-25 to Dolphins and drop to 2-5
stories.summary: The Jets lost at home on Oct. 25 despite 287 passing yards from Geno Smith and 104 rushing yards from Braelon Allen. Defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat left with a knee injury late in the second quarter and did not return.

stories.text: Sweat and Ossai out, Bailey doubtful against Las Vegas
stories.summary: Edge Joseph Ossai (ankle), lineman Max Mitchell (concussion) and tackle T'Vondre Sweat (knee) are out. Edge David Bailey (groin) is doubtful. Running back Breece Hall (quad) and lineman Dylan Parham (knee) are questionable.

stories.text: Geno Smith throws for 287 yards and three scores in defeat
stories.summary: Smith completed 23 of 30 passes with three touchdowns and one interception against Miami. On the season he has completed 145 of 207 passes, and his 105.2 passer rating ranks sixth in the NFL.

stories.text: 8: completions of 40-plus yards for Geno Smith through seven games
stories.summary: Smith has spread those eight deep completions among six receivers. No Jets quarterback had reached that mark in a team's first seven games since Joe Namath in 1972.

stories.text: Raiders at MetLife Stadium, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Jets (2-5) host Las Vegas on Nov. 1. Watch how the defense line holds up with Ossai and Sweat out and Bailey doubtful, and whether Hall is cleared to play.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens need Lamar back to stop the skid

stories.text: Ravens sit last in the AFC North and visit a 5-1 Bills team
stories.summary: Baltimore enters Week 8 at 4-3 after back-to-back losses to AFC North rivals, one game behind first-place Cleveland. The Ravens went 1-2 with Tyler Huntley in place of Lamar Jackson. Sunday's trip to Buffalo gives them a chance to stop the slide against a Bills defense that ranks in the bottom three in total, scoring and passing defense.

stories.text: Lamar Jackson practiced fully and is set to return from a high ankle sprain
stories.summary: Jackson took full reps Wednesday and Thursday and practiced again Friday after missing three games. Coach Jesse Minter said the team expects to have him. The league's Week 8 report lists guard Olaivavega Ioane and safety Jaylinn Hawkins out, with running back Adam Randall (neck) and cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee) questionable.

stories.text: Lamar Jackson comes back with a 70.8 percent completion rate
stories.summary: Before the ankle injury, Jackson completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception. He added 144 yards and a score on 19 carries. The Ravens have not seen the running mobility they want from him in practice, so watch how freely he moves Sunday.

stories.text: 14 to 5: Ravens touchdowns with Jackson on the field versus off it
stories.summary: Baltimore scored 14 touchdowns in the 14 quarters Jackson played this season. In the 14 quarters he missed, the offense found the end zone five times. The gap explains why the Ravens went 1-2 without him.

stories.text: Ravens at Bills, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Baltimore (4-3) visits Buffalo (5-1), where the Bills are 3-point favorites in ESPN's listing. The Ravens have not allowed 100 rushing yards to a running back in 21 straight games, and they face James Cook, who averages 104.5 rushing yards per game. After Buffalo they play Jacksonville, the Chargers, Carolina and Houston before a Week 13 bye.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Burrow rolls into Titans game on a hot streak

stories.text: Bengals erase a 13-0 halftime hole and bury Baltimore 35-13
stories.summary: Cincinnati trailed 13-0 at the half, then scored 35 straight points to beat the Ravens and pick up its first AFC North win of the year. The defense shut Baltimore out after the break. The Bengals now host a 1-6 Titans team as heavy favorites.

stories.text: Safety Kyle Dugger is out; two players land on injured reserve
stories.summary: The league's Week 8 report lists safety Kyle Dugger (quadriceps) out and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) questionable. Tight end Tanner Hudson and Erick All Jr. went on injured reserve after the Baltimore game. The team did not describe either injury in its postgame notes.

stories.text: Tee Higgins posts 148 yards and a score against the Ravens
stories.summary: Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown in Baltimore. It was the 17th 100-yard game of his career, and his career total reached 6,012 receiving yards in 91 games. Mike Gesicki also scored for the fourth straight game and has five touchdowns this season.

stories.text: 249: Burrow's second-half passing yards, all four touchdowns
stories.summary: Joe Burrow went 16 of 18 for 249 yards and all four of his touchdown passes after halftime in Baltimore. He is the only quarterback this season with four touchdown passes in a single half. He now has back-to-back games with four touchdowns and no interceptions, and another would tie the longest such streak in league history.

stories.text: Titans at Bengals, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cincinnati (4-2) hosts Tennessee (1-6) at Paycor Stadium and is a 10-point favorite in ESPN's listing. The Titans play their first game since trading Jeffery Simmons to the Bears. Watch whether Burrow can extend his streak of four-touchdown games.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns chase a sweep of Pittsburgh

stories.text: Browns lead the division and can sweep the Steelers for the first time since 1988
stories.summary: Cleveland sits at 5-2 after a walk-off field goal in Tennessee, tying its best start since 1999. A win in Pittsburgh would complete the sweep. The Browns have not won there since 2003, a streak of 22 straight losses.

stories.text: Tackle Tytus Howard sits in the concussion protocol and is questionable
stories.summary: Right tackle Tytus Howard missed a third straight practice and has not cleared the concussion protocol. Defensive back Myles Harden (hamstring) and safety Daniel Thomas (ankle) are also questionable. Defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. is expected back, and coach Todd Monken has not decided whether Dillon Gabriel will be active behind Shedeur Sanders.

stories.text: Deshaun Watson throws for 308 yards, his first 300-yard game in Cleveland
stories.summary: Watson completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards and ran for a 9-yard touchdown in the 27-24 win over Tennessee. He went 3 of 3 for 50 yards on the game-winning drive. Cleveland finished with 491 net yards, a season high.

stories.text: 22: straight Browns losses in Pittsburgh since 2003
stories.summary: Cleveland has not won a regular-season game at the Steelers' home since 2003. The Browns have still covered five straight division games, all as underdogs, since Week 11 last season. Kicker Andre Szmyt has hit three game-winners this season.

stories.text: Browns at Steelers, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Both teams are 5-2 and the game decides first place in the AFC North. Pittsburgh is a 3.5-point favorite in ESPN's listing. Watch Cleveland's interior line, which has rarely been whole since September, against the Steelers' run game.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers carry a three-game streak into Cleveland game

stories.text: Steelers win three straight, but the schedule has been soft
stories.summary: Pittsburgh beat the Colts, the Buccaneers and the Saints (16-10 in Paris) to reach 5-2. Each opponent has only two wins. Sports Illustrated argues the defense is carrying the team while Aaron Rodgers struggles to push the ball downfield.

stories.text: Two corners out, Jalen Ramsey cleared and Skowronek questionable
stories.summary: Cornerbacks Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter (both hamstring) are out after missing every practice. Jalen Ramsey practiced fully Thursday and Friday and will play with a wrist injury. Receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) was limited all week and is questionable.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren runs for 101 yards on 18 carries against the Saints
stories.summary: Warren carried the offense in Paris with 18 rushes for 101 yards while the passing game sputtered. Rodgers finished 19 of 30 for 212 yards and one touchdown. DK Metcalf caught two passes for 56 yards.

stories.text: 27th: where the Steelers rank in red zone scoring
stories.summary: Pittsburgh ranks 27th in red zone scoring even with three straight wins. The offense has converted 45.24 percent of its third downs over those three games. Stalled drives near the goal line are the clearest limit on this offense.

stories.text: Browns at Steelers, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh hosts Cleveland with both teams at 5-2 and first place in the division at stake. The Steelers are 3.5-point favorites in ESPN's listing. Cleveland beat them 27-24 earlier this season, so Pittsburgh is playing for the split.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans hit the bye at 2-5 with defense to fix

stories.text: Texans fall 27-21 in overtime to Giants, sink to 2-5
stories.summary: Houston gave up a 30-yard Devin Singletary run in overtime and lost to the Giants. The Giants ran for a season-high 188 yards, and coach DeMeco Ryans said the tackling was not good enough. The Texans now take their bye with the defense that led the league last year looking lost.

stories.text: Texans put WR Jaylin Noel on IR with turf toe
stories.summary: Noel hurt his toe on a fourth-quarter kick return against the Giants and is expected to miss the rest of the season. Houston placed him on injured reserve Wednesday and signed running back Emari Demercado to fill the roster spot. Noel led the team with 331 receiving yards, so the passing game loses its top yardage producer.

stories.text: C.J. Stroud ranks fourth in passing yards despite 2-5
stories.summary: Stroud has 1,867 passing yards, 11 touchdowns and one interception through seven games, fourth most in the league. His best game came in the 34-31 win over Jacksonville: 312 yards, three touchdowns and a 116.3 passer rating. Extension talks wait until the offseason.

stories.text: 342: yards per game the Texans defense now allows
stories.summary: Houston's defense gives up 342 yards a game this season. Last year it allowed 277.2 and led the NFL. The Giants' 188 rushing yards on Sunday showed where the slide started.

stories.text: Bye in Week 8, then the Chargers on Nov. 8
stories.summary: Houston is off this weekend and returns Nov. 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers. The bye gives the staff time to fix the tackling and decide how to replace Noel. Tank Dell, back after 22 months away, should see more snaps.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts trade Nelson and Buckner, rebuild is on

stories.text: Colts trade Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner
stories.summary: Indianapolis sent Buckner to San Francisco for a 2027 fourth-round pick and Nelson to Seattle for a 2027 third and a 2028 fifth. Assistant GM Ed Dodds ran the deals after the team fired GM Chris Ballard last week. Both players were in the final year of their contracts, and the Colts are on a three-game losing streak.

stories.text: Boettcher and Walley sit out Thursday practice
stories.summary: Linebacker Bryce Boettcher (groin) and cornerback Justin Walley (knee) did not practice Thursday. Tight ends Tyler Warren (groin) and Drew Ogletree (knee) were limited. Sauce Gardner (calf) and receiver Anthony Gould (concussion) practiced in full.

stories.text: Josh Downs asks for a trade as the rebuild begins
stories.summary: Downs, in the final year of his rookie deal, requested a trade, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. He has 26 catches for 307 yards and no touchdowns, with a career-low 56.5 percent catch rate. Downs said he is open to whatever comes his way.

stories.text: 108: passing yards for Daniel Jones in loss to Minnesota
stories.summary: Jones threw for 108 yards and an interception in the 16-10 loss to the Vikings. Indianapolis has lost three straight, two of them by one possession. The offense will face a Jaguars team that has won every home meeting in the series since 2014.

stories.text: At Jacksonville, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Colts visit EverBank Stadium to face the 4-2 Jaguars. Watch how the roster holds up after the Nelson and Buckner trades, and whether the run defense can slow Jacksonville. Rain is possible.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars lead the South and host Colts after bye

stories.text: Rested Jaguars lead the South and host the Colts
stories.summary: Jacksonville comes out of its bye at 4-2 and atop the division. The Jaguars split two games in London, beating Philadelphia and losing to Houston. Coach Liam Coen said 56 players came in to lift on the off day, the most he has had.

stories.text: Safety Antonio Johnson out with ankle injury
stories.summary: Johnson hurt his ankle in the loss to Houston in London and did not practice this week, so he sits out Sunday. Receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring) is questionable. Long snapper Ross Matiscik and cornerback Montaric Brown are expected back.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence threw 300 yards in back-to-back games
stories.summary: Lawrence has 14 touchdown passes and four interceptions through six games. He has topped 300 yards in each of his last two outings and averages 246 passing yards a game. He is 7-2 against Indianapolis.

stories.text: 4th: Jaguars' league rank in dropback EPA
stories.summary: Jacksonville ranks fourth in dropback EPA at 0.227 and tenth in dropback success rate at 49.1 percent, per rbsdm.com through Thursday. Indianapolis ranks 19th in dropback EPA allowed. The Colts do rank seventh in dropback success rate allowed.

stories.text: Colts at EverBank, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Jacksonville hosts Indianapolis in its second straight division game. The Jaguars have won 11 straight home games in the series, but they are 2-6 in games right after a bye since 2018. Watch their run defense and their turnover count, since they have one takeaway in two games.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans blow a 14-0 lead, now visit Cincinnati

stories.text: Titans lose 27-24 to Browns on last-second field goal
stories.summary: Tennessee led Cleveland 14-0 and still lost when a 32-yard field goal went through as time expired. The Titans fell to 1-6 and now travel to Cincinnati. The defense did force five turnovers over its last two games.

stories.text: Spears, Tate and Townsend out against Cincinnati
stories.summary: Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), rookie receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) are out. Calvin Ridley (hip), John Franklin-Myers (groin) and Jaylon Jones (knee) are questionable. Without Tate, Ridley, Elic Ayomanor and Wan'Dale Robinson carry the receiving load.

stories.text: Tony Pollard runs for 129 yards and three scores
stories.summary: Pollard carried 25 times for 129 yards and three touchdowns against Cleveland, matching his career high in scores. He opened the game with a 36-yard touchdown run and finished with 155 scrimmage yards. He ranks ninth in the league with 478 rushing yards.

stories.text: 5.7: Cam Ward's yards per attempt, 32nd of 33 QBs
stories.summary: Ward has 1,179 passing yards and averages 5.7 yards per attempt, second to last among eligible quarterbacks. Tennessee's offense ranks 31st in points (15.4) and last in yards (248.6) per game. Defenses pressure him on 35.5 percent of dropbacks.

stories.text: At Cincinnati, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Titans face the 4-2 Bengals, who rank fourth in scoring at 27.2 points a game. Joe Burrow has 15 touchdowns and three interceptions. Tennessee then has its Week 9 bye before it hosts Jacksonville on Nov. 15.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos chase revenge and the division lead

stories.text: Broncos get their shot at Kansas City with the AFC West on the line
stories.summary: Denver hosts the 5-1 Chiefs on Sunday and can take a half-game lead in the division with a win. Kansas City beat the Broncos 31-10 in Week 1, a result Sean Payton called a slap in the face. Denver has won four of the last six meetings and beat Arizona 30-16 last week.

stories.text: Hufanga and Harvey out, four Broncos questionable vs. Chiefs
stories.summary: Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and running back RJ Harvey (knee) are out. Tackle Garett Bolles (hip), lineman Zach Allen (hamstring), receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) and safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) are questionable. Cornerback Pat Surtain II practiced fully on Friday and is on track to return after missing three games.

stories.text: Alex Singleton leads the league in tackles and earns AFC honors
stories.summary: Linebacker Alex Singleton made 19 stops against Arizona and won his first career AFC Defensive Player of the Week award. He now leads the NFL with 87 tackles. Denver's defense ranks fourth in EPA allowed.

stories.text: 20: straight home games with multiple sacks for Denver
stories.summary: The Broncos have recorded at least two sacks in 20 consecutive home games, the fourth-longest streak in NFL history. They have held opponents to 17 points or fewer in three straight games. Kansas City has only eight sacks of its own through six games.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Denver on Sunday for a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City comes to Mile High for a game that decides first place in the division. Payton will coach his 300th NFL game, and a win gives him his 200th. Watch how Bo Nix, who completes 59.2 percent of his throws, handles a Chiefs defense that ranks fifth in EPA allowed.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs look to bounce back at Denver

stories.text: Chiefs arrive in Denver after a 20-3 loss at Seattle
stories.summary: Kansas City's only loss came last week, and Patrick Mahomes had his worst game of the season: 19 of 33 for 165 yards and an interception. He is working back from a knee injury suffered in December and has gone consecutive games without a touchdown pass for the first time in his career. A win in Denver would give the Chiefs control of the AFC West.

stories.text: Delane and Sneed questionable, Norman-Lott out for Denver
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) is out. Cornerbacks Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and L'Jarius Sneed (knee) are questionable, and edge rusher R. Mason Thomas is questionable for personal reasons. Mahomes, Travis Kelce, Creed Humphrey and Nick Bolton all practiced fully on Friday.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker III carries the Kansas City offense
stories.summary: Walker has 701 rushing yards and averages 5.8 yards per carry. He ran for 173 yards against Denver in September and piled up a career-best 191 scrimmage yards in that game. The Chiefs lean on him while the passing game searches for rhythm.

stories.text: 15,143: Kelce's record for tight end receiving yards
stories.summary: Travis Kelce passed Tony Gonzalez last week for the most receiving yards by a tight end in NFL history, playoffs included. At 37, Kelce averages 14.3 yards per catch, his best mark in 14 seasons.

stories.text: Chiefs at Broncos, Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City leads the all-time series 74-59 and won 31-10 in Week 1. Watch whether Chris Jones, who has only a half-sack this season, can pressure Bo Nix. The Chiefs are a 1.5-point favorite in the ESPN listing.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders stay with Cousins, chase a win

stories.text: Raiders back Kirk Cousins through a four-game losing streak
stories.summary: Las Vegas started 3-0 and has lost four straight. Coach Klint Kubiak said there is no quarterback controversy, so rookie Fernando Mendoza keeps waiting. The defense has allowed 35.8 points per game during the skid.

stories.text: Johnson out; Powers-Johnson and Bech questionable at the Jets
stories.summary: Defensive end Patrick Johnson (stinger) and tight end Carter Runyon (foot) are out. Guard Jackson Powers-Johnson (back) and receiver Jack Bech (forearm) are questionable. Tight end Brock Bowers (calf) carries no game designation.

stories.text: Cousins keeps producing despite the losses
stories.summary: Cousins has 16 touchdowns and 5 interceptions this season. He threw for 295 yards and two touchdowns in last week's 35-21 loss to the Rams. The Raiders score 26.1 points per game, seventh in the league.

stories.text: 35.8: points per game Las Vegas has allowed during the skid
stories.summary: Over the four straight losses, the Raiders have given up 416.5 yards and 35.8 points per game. The Rams ran for 199 yards against them last week. The Raiders' defense allows 28.1 points per game for the season, fourth-most in the league.

stories.text: Raiders at Jets, Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Las Vegas visits the 2-5 Jets at MetLife Stadium looking to end its losing streak. Watch the run defense, which has allowed 164 rushing yards per game since Week 4, and Bowers' calf. The Jets will miss nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers face the Rams after bye

stories.text: Winless Chargers keep McDaniel calling plays after the bye
stories.summary: Los Angeles is 0-6 and the league's only winless team. Jim Harbaugh said Mike McDaniel will keep calling the offensive plays. The offense averages 15.0 points per game, last in the NFL.

stories.text: Derwin James out; McConkey cleared to play against Rams
stories.summary: Safety Derwin James Jr. (hamstring), guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), receiver Brenen Thompson and defensive back Deane Leonard (concussion) are out. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley (both hamstring) are questionable. Receiver Ladd McConkey practiced fully all week and came off the report with a concussion no longer listed.

stories.text: Cornerback Tarheeb Still holds up in coverage
stories.summary: Still has played all six games with 22 tackles, a tackle for loss, a forced fumble and three passes defensed. He has allowed 8.1 yards per reception, 11th among cornerbacks targeted at least 15 times. Pro Football Focus lists his completion percentage allowed as the lowest of his career.

stories.text: 15.0: points per game, last in the NFL
stories.summary: The Chargers also rank last in EPA per play and success rate and have 15 turnovers. The defense, under first-year coordinator Chris O'Leary, ranks sixth in success rate. That gap explains how a team with a strong defense sits at 0-6.

stories.text: Chargers at Rams, Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays at SoFi Stadium in the Battle of Los Angeles against the 3-4 Rams, who are 6.5-point favorites. The Chargers run defense, which allows 123.8 yards per game, faces the Rams' backs. Tackle Joe Alt returns from a neck injury.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys run wild, host Cardinals Sunday

stories.text: Cowboys ground Eagles for 204 rushing yards
stories.summary: Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-21 on Monday night and moved to 3-4. The Cowboys ran 38 times for 204 yards and piled up 416 total yards, a season best. They scored on seven of nine possessions.

stories.text: Turpin and Winters out, Pickens questionable
stories.summary: Receiver KaVontae Turpin and linebacker Dee Winters will miss Sunday's game. George Pickens is questionable with a shoulder and hamstring issue after limited work Friday. Tight end Luke Schoonmaker is likely out with a groin injury, so fullback Hunter Luepke could see more snaps.

stories.text: Javonte Williams posts a career-high 155 yards
stories.summary: Williams carried 25 times for 155 yards against Philadelphia and added a 2-yard touchdown to close the game. It was the biggest rushing day by a Cowboys back since Ezekiel Elliott gained 159 in December 2016. He also broke a 34-yard run in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: 204: rushing yards for a team that ranked 30th
stories.summary: Dallas came into Monday night 30th in the league at 76 rushing yards per game. The Cowboys then ran for 204 on 5.4 yards per carry, well above their 3.7 season average. Dak Prescott also threw three touchdown passes with no interceptions.

stories.text: Cardinals visit AT&T Stadium Sunday at 1 p.m.
stories.summary: Dallas hosts Arizona (2-5) on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. The Cowboys are seeking their first winning streak of the season and have not beaten the Cardinals since 2017. Dallas then travels to face the Indianapolis Colts.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants lead the East heading into the bye

stories.text: Giants hold first place at 4-2-1 entering bye
stories.summary: New York beat Houston 27-21 in overtime and sits atop the NFC East with a two-game edge in the win column. The Giants have won with three different quarterbacks in their first seven games, a first since starts were tracked in 1950. They use the bye week to heal before two division games.

stories.text: Tracy to IR, Edmunds done for the year
stories.summary: Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. went on injured reserve with a hamstring injury and will miss at least four games. Linebacker Tremaine Edmunds is out for the season with a torn chest muscle. Quarterback Jaxson Dart is also out for the year.

stories.text: Skattebo rushes for 124 yards in overtime win
stories.summary: Cam Skattebo carried 17 times for 124 yards and a 16-yard touchdown against Houston. His 42-yard run in overtime set up Devin Singletary's winning 30-yard score. Houston allowed a season-high 188 rushing yards.

stories.text: 4: straight 100-yard games for Malik Nabers
stories.summary: Nabers caught seven passes for 111 yards against the Texans. That makes four straight games over 100 yards, and he leads the league in receiving over that span. J.J. McCarthy threw to him in his first start of the season, going 20 of 28 for 252 yards.

stories.text: Bye, then Eagles Nov. 8 and Washington Nov. 12
stories.summary: The Giants are on bye in Week 8. They visit Philadelphia on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX, then host Washington on Thursday, Nov. 12, at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. John Harbaugh is 15-3 in games right after a bye.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles seek a win at Washington on Sunday night

stories.text: Eagles chase a win with McKee under center
stories.summary: Philadelphia has lost five straight, most recently 38-21 to Dallas on Monday night. Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve, so Tanner McKee is set to start. Coach Nick Sirianni says the young players are getting real reps and improving.

stories.text: Barkley cleared, DeVonta Smith ruled out
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley practiced on a limited basis Friday and will play despite hamstring and back injuries. DeVonta Smith is out with a hamstring injury after missing practice two weeks running. Britain Covey, Jonathan Jones, Dontayvion Wicks and Jihaad Campbell are also out.

stories.text: Makai Lemon finds the end zone against Dallas
stories.summary: The No. 1 pick caught seven passes for 67 yards and a touchdown in the loss to the Cowboys. He scored on a 4-yard pass from McKee in the third quarter. With Smith out, he figures to carry a bigger load in Washington.

stories.text: 5.7: Barkley's yards per carry, second in the NFL
stories.summary: Barkley averages 5.7 yards per carry, behind only Kansas City's Kenneth Walker at 5.8. He had 72 total yards and a touchdown on nine touches against Dallas before aggravating his hamstring. Washington's defense allows touchdowns on a league-worst 81.8 percent of red zone trips.

stories.text: At Commanders, Sunday night at 8:20 on NBC
stories.summary: The Eagles visit Washington at Northwest Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Philadelphia won the Week 1 meeting 24-22. Watch McKee's timing with his receivers and how the run defense answers a rough night against Dallas.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders return from bye as healthiest in weeks

stories.text: Commanders need wins after the bye week
stories.summary: Washington sits at 1-4-1 and 0-2-1 in the division, 2.5 games behind the Giants. Dan Quinn's job security is a talking point, though sources say there is no immediate danger. The next three games, against the Eagles, Rams and Giants, could shape the season.

stories.text: Payne questionable, Kinlaw out vs. Eagles
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Daron Payne (foot) is questionable and Javon Kinlaw (knee) is out. Treylon Burks, John Bates and Jer'Zhan Newton are also questionable. Jayden Daniels (left elbow) practiced fully, and the team calls itself the healthiest it has been in weeks.

stories.text: Daniels piles up yards in his last two games
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels threw for 499 yards and two touchdowns over his last two games, and ran for 113 yards and two more scores. He plays in a brace on the left elbow he dislocated in Week 2. He has taken a hit on 27.3 percent of his dropbacks, third-highest in the league.

stories.text: +6: Washington's turnover margin
stories.summary: The Commanders sit at plus-6 in turnover differential and have turned the ball over only twice in six games. They still trail the field in discipline, with a penalty on 25 of their 69 drives. Terry McLaurin is out for the season with a torn patellar tendon.

stories.text: Eagles at Northwest Stadium, Sunday at 8:20 on NBC
stories.summary: Washington hosts Philadelphia on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. The Commanders lost the Week 1 meeting 24-22 and blitz on 43.9 percent of snaps, second-most in the league. Watch whether Daniels protects the ball and the red zone defense tightens up.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Hot Williams meets Seattle's top defense

stories.text: Caleb Williams brings a hot arm into Seattle on Monday night
stories.summary: Williams has thrown for 300-plus yards in back-to-back games since he came back from a hamstring injury. He put up 308 yards and two touchdowns in last week's 30-24 win over the Patriots. Now he faces a Seahawks defense that leads the league in yards allowed.

stories.text: Monangai still out of practice, Loveland added with neck issue
stories.summary: Running back Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) sat out again Friday and has not played since the Week 4 win over the Jets. Tight end Colston Loveland joined the report with a neck injury after a limited practice, and linebacker D'Marco Jackson (ankle) did not practice. Final designations come after Saturday's session.

stories.text: D'Andre Swift carries the league's top rushing attack
stories.summary: Swift has 628 rushing yards and seven touchdowns through seven games. He fronts an offense that leads the NFL in rushing. Seattle has not allowed a 100-yard rusher in 36 straight games, so something has to give Monday.

stories.text: 154.3: Chicago's rushing yards per game lead the NFL
stories.summary: No team runs for more yards per game than the Bears at 154.3. The defense backs it up by holding opponents to a 26 percent conversion rate on third down. That pairing sets up a physical matchup with Seattle.

stories.text: Bears at Seahawks, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET on ABC
stories.summary: Chicago (5-2) visits Seattle (4-3) on Monday Night Football, with the Seahawks favored by three. Watch whether the Bears' run game cracks a defense that has not allowed a 100-yard rusher in 36 games. Jaxon Smith-Njigba leads the league with 123.9 receiving yards per game.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions host unbeaten Vikings at Ford Field

stories.text: Lions get first shot at the NFL's lone unbeaten team
stories.summary: Detroit hosts 6-0 Minnesota on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET in a game that reshapes the NFC North. The Lions rank second in offensive EPA. The Vikings won both meetings last season, sacking Jared Goff ten times and forcing seven turnovers.

stories.text: Kerby Joseph out, Roger McCreary questionable for Vikings
stories.summary: Safety Kerby Joseph (knee) is out after three limited practices, and Dan Campbell is easing him back. Cornerback Roger McCreary (foot) is questionable. Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Penei Sewell all practiced fully Friday.

stories.text: Goff owns the league's best grade against the blitz
stories.summary: Jared Goff leads the NFL in PFF grade against the blitz, which matters because Minnesota blitzes more than any team. Detroit's offense ranks second in both points and yards per game. Goff needs to read pressure quickly Sunday.

stories.text: 391: Lions defense gives up the most yards per game
stories.summary: Detroit allows 391 yards per game, the most in the NFL, even as the offense ranks near the top in every category. Joseph's absence leaves the secondary thin. Minnesota's offense is far weaker than its record, so the matchup tests the Lions' weak side against a modest attack.

stories.text: Vikings at Lions, Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Minnesota visits Ford Field on Sunday, with Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady on the call. Watch Aidan Hutchinson against the Vikings' protection and how Detroit covers without Joseph. The Vikings lead the all-time series 82-45-2.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers beat Panthers but nearly blow big lead

stories.text: Packers top Panthers 27-19 after a late scare
stories.summary: Green Bay led 27-10 in the third quarter and then watched Carolina close the gap. The Panthers outgained the Packers 109 to 32 in the fourth quarter. The win lifts Green Bay to 5-3, but the late slide is the talking point.

stories.text: Watson cleared after chest scare, Parsons still on PUP
stories.summary: Christian Watson left Thursday's game by ambulance with a chest injury, got cleared by doctors and returned to make a key catch late. Micah Parsons remains on the PUP list. Matt LaFleur said there is a chance Parsons returns to practice soon, but he is highly unlikely to play Week 9.

stories.text: Watson posts 113 yards on eight catches
stories.summary: Watson caught eight passes on ten targets for 113 yards, the most catches and yards of any receiver in the game. Matthew Golden added seven catches for 79 yards and a touchdown. Jordan Love threw for 288 yards and three scores.

stories.text: 6: Different Packers recorded sacks of Bryce Young
stories.summary: Ty'Ron Hopper, Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Dani Dennis-Sutton, Brenton Cox Jr. and Devonte Wyatt each got to Young, who went down six times. The front is producing without Parsons on the field.

stories.text: Packers visit the Patriots on November 8
stories.summary: Green Bay played Thursday, so it has no game this weekend. Its Week 9 game is at New England on November 8. The source does not give a kickoff time or network.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings head to Detroit

stories.text: Vikings carry the league's only perfect record into Detroit
stories.summary: Minnesota is 6-0 and the NFL's lone unbeaten team, but the offense ranks 31st in EPA. The defense ranks first in EPA and blitzes more than anyone. Sunday at Ford Field tests whether that formula holds against the Lions' second-ranked offense.

stories.text: Vikings expect a full, healthy roster for Detroit
stories.summary: Minnesota reported a clean injury sheet heading into Sunday and expects its full active roster. Justin Jefferson missed one full game and most of another earlier this season with a sprained left ankle.

stories.text: Jefferson says winning beats stats amid quiet season
stories.summary: Jefferson has 23 catches through seven weeks, his lowest total at this point of any season. He averages 60.4 receiving yards per game. He told reporters he cares more about wins and accepts that the offense needs to improve.

stories.text: 31st: Vikings rank near the bottom in offensive EPA at 6-0
stories.summary: Minnesota sits 31st in offensive EPA despite an unbeaten record. The defense, first in defensive EPA, carries the team. Lions and Vikings split the profile: Detroit scores, Minnesota stops.

stories.text: Vikings at Lions, Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Minnesota plays at Ford Field on Sunday with Kyler Murray at quarterback. The Vikings won both meetings with Detroit last season and lead the all-time series 82-45-2. Watch Murray against a Lions defense that gives up the most yards per game in the league.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons ride the 49ers upset into Tampa

stories.text: Falcons knock off unbeaten 49ers, 29-20
stories.summary: Atlanta beat previously undefeated San Francisco at home on October 25 and forced four takeaways to do it. The offense has averaged 31.0 points over its last five games with Michael Penix Jr. back under center. The win moved the Falcons to 3-4 and kept them in the NFC South race.

stories.text: Brian Robinson Jr. out again, eight Falcons questionable
stories.summary: Running back Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) is the only Falcon ruled out for Sunday, and he will miss his second straight game. Eight players carry a questionable tag, including defensive end Samson Ebukam, defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. and linebacker Divine Deablo. Guard Chris Lindstrom did not practice Friday for a personal reason.

stories.text: Penix named NFC Offensive Player of the Week
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. threw touchdown passes to Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Nick Muse against San Francisco without an interception. The league named him NFC Offensive Player of the Week. Penix is working back from a 2025 ACL tear and has now led the offense through five starts.

stories.text: 31.0: Falcons points per game over the last five weeks
stories.summary: Atlanta has scored 31.0 points per game across its last five outings. Bijan Robinson has 907 yards from scrimmage through seven games, including 122 against San Francisco. The Falcons rank fourth in rushing offense at 149.5 yards per game.

stories.text: Falcons visit Tampa Bay Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Atlanta (3-4) plays at Raymond James Stadium against a Buccaneers team that sits at 2-5. Tampa Bay owns the league's second-best run defense, so Robinson and the Falcons ground game face a real test. Watch Kyle Pitts too: he caught 11 passes for 166 yards and three touchdowns against the Bucs last year.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers drop two in four days, line in tatters

stories.text: Panthers fall to 3-4 after 27-19 loss in Green Bay
stories.summary: Carolina lost on Thursday night to the Packers four days after a 43-13 home loss to Tampa Bay. Bryce Young went 23 of 41 for 209 yards with one touchdown and one interception, and the Panthers converted only 5 of 18 third downs. Green Bay's pass rush sacked him six times.

stories.text: Secondary and offensive line thin after Green Bay
stories.summary: Cornerback Will Lee III left Thursday's game in the second quarter with a hamstring injury. Cornerbacks Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson and Akayleb Evans were already out, and linemen Damien Lewis and Taylor Moton were hurt before the game. Carolina has until November 8 to heal up.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard carries the offense in Green Bay
stories.summary: Chuba Hubbard ran 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown against the Packers. He scored from one yard out after a fourth-down conversion to give Carolina a 10-6 lead in the second quarter. The ground game was the only steady piece of an offense that managed 258 total yards.

stories.text: 133: pressures Bryce Young has faced, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Young has faced the most pressures in the league and the most quick pressures, at 80. His net yards per attempt dropped from 7.4 through six weeks to 4.5 over the last two games. Injuries to Ikem Ekwonu, Damien Lewis and Taylor Moton have left the line short of starters.

stories.text: No game this weekend; Broncos visit November 8
stories.summary: Carolina already played its Week 8 game on Thursday, so it has no game Sunday or Monday. The Panthers host Denver in Week 9 on Sunday, November 8, at 1:00 p.m. on CBS. Watch whether any of the missing linemen and cornerbacks return by then.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints hit the bye at 2-5 looking for answers

stories.text: Saints reach the bye at 2-5 with no easy fix
stories.summary: New Orleans trails in every game it plays and has won only twice from behind. Owner Gayle Benson said publicly after the Week 5 loss to Minnesota that she was unhappy with the team. Coach Kellen Moore says he will spend the bye hunting for ways to score more.

stories.text: Bye gives Saints time to heal, with several on IR
stories.summary: Running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. are on injured reserve and eligible to return when practice resumes. Safety Justin Reid is in concussion protocol after leaving the Pittsburgh game, and guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) was trending toward a return. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) remains on IR and has yet to play.

stories.text: Tyler Shough has thrown for 1,721 yards through seven
stories.summary: Shough has completed 183 of 273 passes for 1,721 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions. He has done it while playing through an injured left hand. Chris Olave leads the team with 49 catches for 636 yards.

stories.text: 44-6: how the Saints have been outscored in first quarters
stories.summary: New Orleans has given up 44 first-quarter points and scored six. The run game is part of the problem: the Saints average 3.5 yards per carry and managed 18 yards on 17 carries in the 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh in Paris. They rank 28th in rushing and 29th in run defense.

stories.text: Saints are on bye, then host Cleveland November 8
stories.summary: New Orleans has no game this week. It returns to the Superdome on Sunday, November 8, against the Browns. Watch how many injured starters practice when work resumes after the bye.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs chase first home win of 2026 against Atlanta

stories.text: Bucs seek first home win after 43-13 rout of Carolina
stories.summary: Tampa Bay won its second straight road game in Week 7 and picked up its first NFC South victory of the year. The Bucs have not won at home yet, and Baker Mayfield says the team must get its mojo back there. A win Sunday over Atlanta would put them at 3-5 and back in the division hunt.

stories.text: Egbuka out with foot injury, Gainwell and Goedeke questionable
stories.summary: Receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot) did not practice Friday and is ruled out against Atlanta. Running back Kenny Gainwell (hip) and tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) are questionable. Baker Mayfield (thumb) and Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) practiced fully all week with no designation.

stories.text: Bucky Irving runs for 106 yards and two scores
stories.summary: Irving carried 24 times for 106 yards and two touchdowns in the win at Carolina. He leads the Bucs with 558 rushing yards and five touchdowns on the season. Mayfield, back from injury, needed only 64 passing yards and a touchdown that day.

stories.text: 258: rushing yards for Tampa Bay at Carolina
stories.summary: The Bucs ran for 258 yards and three touchdowns against the Panthers. They rank third in the league at 146.4 rushing yards per game, and their defense ranks second against the run. They have also recorded five sacks in each of the last two games.

stories.text: Falcons come to Raymond James Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tampa Bay hosts Atlanta in a game that matters to the NFC South standings. The forecast calls for humidity and a high chance of rain, which favors the run game. Watch Pitts, who caught three touchdowns against the Bucs last year.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Brissett stays the starter in Dallas

stories.text: Cardinals stick with Brissett as they chase a win in Dallas
stories.summary: Arizona fell 30-16 to Denver last Sunday and sits at 2-5. Coach Mike LaFleur confirmed Jacoby Brissett starts at Dallas, which pushes back the debut of rookie Carson Beck. The offense has struggled to produce big plays in the air or on the ground.

stories.text: Gaines and Nolen out, three Cardinals questionable for Dallas
stories.summary: Right guard Jon Gaines II (ankle) and defensive lineman Walter Nolen III (ankle) will not play. Guard Hjalte Froholdt (knee), cornerback Max Melton (knee) and safety Andrew Wingard (knee) are questionable. Froholdt missed Friday's practice, so Hayden Conner could slide to center if he sits.

stories.text: Trey McBride keeps piling up catches
stories.summary: McBride leads Arizona with 59 receptions for 472 yards and four touchdowns, and the offense has targeted him 77 times. He has caught at least seven passes in all seven games. That streak is the longest to open a season by a tight end in league history.

stories.text: 1-for-10: Arizona's red zone mark over its last two games
stories.summary: The Cardinals have turned only one of ten recent red zone trips into a touchdown, the second-worst rate in the league over that span. They have leaned on kicker Chad Ryland to cover for it. Fixing that is the clearest path to a win in Dallas.

stories.text: At Dallas on Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Arizona (2-5) visits the 3-4 Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. The Cardinals have won four straight meetings with Dallas. Watch whether Jeremiyah Love, back from a two-game ankle absence, can get the run game moving against the league's second-worst run defense.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams host winless Chargers after Vegas win

stories.text: Rams end their skid and Stafford takes the franchise TD record
stories.summary: Los Angeles beat the Raiders 35-21 in Las Vegas to stop a losing streak. Matthew Stafford threw three touchdown passes, which gave him 155 for his Rams career and moved him past Roman Gabriel's 154. Davis Allen caught two of them, a career high.

stories.text: McDuffie, Parkinson and Shelton questionable vs. Chargers
stories.summary: Cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin), tight end Colby Parkinson (rib), lineman Coleman Shelton (hip) and receiver Jordan Whittington (back) are all questionable. Long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) is doubtful. Puka Nacua, Alaric Jackson and Byron Young sat Friday for rest, not injury.

stories.text: Stafford at 1,989 yards and 14 touchdowns
stories.summary: Stafford has thrown for 1,989 yards, 14 touchdowns and 7 interceptions this season, at 7.2 yards per attempt. He went 23 of 29 for 195 yards and three scores against Las Vegas. Puka Nacua leads the receivers with 45 catches for 485 yards.

stories.text: 80%: Rams' conversion rate on third-and-3 or shorter
stories.summary: That rate is the best in the NFL. Chargers opponents convert only 32% of those short third downs, the lowest mark in the league. The Rams also hold the edge in 11 of 12 head-to-head analytics categories against the 0-6 Chargers.

stories.text: Chargers at SoFi Stadium Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The 3-4 Rams host the 0-6 Chargers, who average a league-low 15 points per game. Los Angeles is a 6.5-point favorite in the ESPN preview. Watch the run game, since Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 192 yards in Las Vegas, with Davante Adams still out after hamstring surgery.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers use the bye to get healthy

stories.text: 49ers take their first loss, then head into the bye
stories.summary: Atlanta beat San Francisco 29-20 after the 49ers led 14-3 early. The turnover count hit four with no takeaways, and Christian McCaffrey left with a hamstring strain. Kyle Shanahan sounded optimistic that McCaffrey can play after the bye.

stories.text: Bosa tracking toward a return, seven players could be back
stories.summary: General manager John Lynch said Nick Bosa is tracking well but must get through a full week of practice first. Shanahan said the team has a good chance of getting seven players back for Week 9. He named receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and DeMarcus Robinson among them.

stories.text: Kaelon Black leads the ground game in Atlanta
stories.summary: Black ran for a team-high 63 yards and scored on a 30-yard run against the Falcons. He also lost a fumble in a game where the 49ers gave the ball away four times. The offense will want that turnover habit fixed before he gets more work.

stories.text: 7: sacks Brock Purdy has taken on 232 dropbacks
stories.summary: The 49ers' offensive line owns the league's lowest pressure rate at 26.7%. It allowed no sacks of Purdy through the first four games, a feat matched only four times since 1990. That protection is a big reason San Francisco reached the bye at 6-1.

stories.text: Bye this week, then the Raiders on Nov. 8
stories.summary: San Francisco is off in Week 8. The 49ers return to host the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium on Nov. 8. Watch which injured starters return to practice first.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks add Quenton Nelson, host Bears

stories.text: Seahawks trade for All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson
stories.summary: Seattle sent Indianapolis a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick for the three-time first-team All-Pro. Nelson is 30 and in the final year of his contract. The line needed help: left tackle Charles Cross is expected to miss a few games with an ankle injury, and the unit gave up 10 sacks in losses to the 49ers and Broncos.

stories.text: Charbonnet expected to make his season debut Monday
stories.summary: Running back Zach Charbonnet is expected to play for the first time this season, after he tore his ACL during last year's playoff run. Earlier reports had pointed to Week 7. Rookie back Jadarian Price has missed four straight games with a chest injury, sits on injured reserve, and is due back at practice this week.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba piles up 150 yards against Kansas City
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba caught for 150 yards in the 20-3 win over the Chiefs, including 129 in the first half, the most in any half of his career. He now has 867 receiving yards and 8 touchdowns, both league highs. ESPN Research says no player since the Super Bowl era began has reached 850 yards and 8 scores through a team's first seven games.

stories.text: 36: straight games without allowing a 100-yard rusher
stories.summary: Seattle's run defense holds the longest such streak in the NFL. It limited Kansas City's Kenneth Walker III to 36 yards on 14 carries and held the Chiefs to 213 total yards. The Seahawks have given up the second-fewest points in the league.

stories.text: Bears at Lumen Field Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: The 4-3 Seahawks host the 5-2 Bears on Monday night. Chicago's defense ranks third in sacks per dropback, and Montez Sweat is back from a two-game suspension. Seattle's reworked line, with Quenton Nelson new to the group, faces its first big test.
